home.title: Spinne Software — the strength is in the structure
home.description: An Italian software company. The best software is not the one that does the most, but the one where everything works as it should. The first is Sparkle.
home.og_title: The strength is in the structure
home.og_description: The best software is not the one that does the most things. It is the one where everything works the way it should. The first product is Sparkle.
home.tw_title: The strength is in the structure
home.tw_description: The best software is not the one that does the most things, but the one where everything works as it should. The first is Sparkle.
home.h1: The strength is in the structure.
home.lede: The best software is not the one that does the most things. It is the one where everything works the way it should.
home.intro_p2: We build our own products with that idea. The first is Sparkle, a video editor that leaves the labour to the machine and the cut to you.
home.sparkle_pull: Creative work should take your time. Not everything around it.
home.sparkle_p1: Editing a video is more than choosing the right shot and making the right cut.
home.sparkle_p2: There is a lot of work in between. Transcribing hours of footage. Removing backgrounds. Keeping a mask on a subject that moves. Making the same adjustment over and over again.
home.sparkle_p3: That work has to be done. It just shouldn't have to take your time.
home.sparkle_p4: Sparkle is a desktop video editor built to handle it for you.
home.sparkle_p5: Its AI works directly inside the editor, taking care of the repetitive parts while you stay focused on the video itself.
home.sparkle_p6: You decide what the video should be. Sparkle helps you get there.
home.h2_ai: Intelligence should help you, not replace you.
home.ai_p1: Sparkle uses AI where it can genuinely save you time.
home.ai_p2: The assistant can work directly on the project, using the editor's own tools. So it can do things you could do yourself, only much faster.
home.ai_p3: And the project stays under your control.
home.ai_p4: You can change what it did. You can carry on from there. You can go back.
home.ai_p5: AI makes the work faster. The decision stays yours.
home.local_p1: Where it can, Sparkle does the work directly on your machine.
home.local_p2: That means many operations can run without uploading your footage to our servers.
home.local_p3: When a feature needs the cloud, we say so plainly.
home.local_p4: We don't want to hide how the product works behind words like "AI-powered" or "intelligent".
home.local_p5: We would rather just tell you what happens.
home.build_p1: We don't think building good software means reinventing everything.
home.build_p2: But we do think the parts that decide how the product feels deserve to be understood and built with care.
home.build_p3: So some things we make ourselves, and others we leave to technology that already exists.
home.build_p4: The choice is not between building everything and using everything. It is knowing where it is worth building. What we use instead is named in full on the
home.one_p1: We don't need to tell you about ten products that might arrive tomorrow.
home.one_p3: We make it work. We improve it. We listen to the people using it.
home.one_p4: Then the next thing will come.
home.one_p5: Not because we have already decided everything we will do over the next five years, but because every product has to be solid enough to become the starting point for what comes after.
home.one_p6: The work first. Then the rest.
home.motto_p1: In Rome, in the Coppedè quarter, stands the Palazzina del Ragno.
home.motto_p2: On its façade, a gilded spider at the centre of its own web.
home.motto_p3: It is a good image for what we want to build: something that takes shape one thread at a time, where every part has its place and adds to the whole.

sparkle.title: Sparkle — a desktop video editor
sparkle.description: A desktop video editor. Background removal, segmentation, depth, mask tracking and transcription run on your own machine. Generative work uses the cloud.
sparkle.og_title: The machine takes the labour. You keep the cut.
sparkle.og_description: Sparkle is a desktop video editor. The AI works inside the editor, so anything it does stays an ordinary change you can undo. In private preview.
sparkle.tw_description: The machine takes the labour. You keep the cut. A desktop video editor, currently in private preview.
sparkle.h1: The machine takes the labour. You keep the cut.
sparkle.lede: Sparkle is a desktop video editor for people who want to spend more time on the video and less on the operations needed to build it.
sparkle.intro_p2: Artificial intelligence can take on the repetitive work directly inside the editor: transcribing speech, isolating a subject, working on masks, and acting on the project when you ask it to.
sparkle.intro_p3: You go on deciding what the video should become.
sparkle.intro_p4: Sparkle does the work. You do the cut.
sparkle.problem_p1: Editing is not just choosing a scene.
sparkle.problem_p2: Before you get to a creative decision there are hours of work: watching the footage, transcribing, preparing the subtitles, isolating a subject, fixing the masks.
sparkle.problem_p3: Sparkle exists to take part of that work off your hands.
sparkle.problem_p4: It does not decide which story to tell for you.
sparkle.problem_p5: It gets you faster to the point where you can decide.
sparkle.h2_ai: The AI works inside the editor.
sparkle.ai_p1: Sparkle does not treat artificial intelligence as a separate tool.
sparkle.ai_p2: The assistant works directly on the project, using the editor's own functions.
sparkle.ai_p3: It can change the cut, work on the clips, and apply operations Sparkle already knows how to run.
sparkle.ai_p4: And when it has finished, what it did stays part of the ordinary project.
sparkle.ai_p5: You can carry on from there, change it, or undo it.
sparkle.ai_p6: No parallel project. No work to rebuild.
sparkle.h2_local: Part of the AI stays on your machine.
sparkle.local_p1: When an operation can run locally, Sparkle can do it directly on your machine.
sparkle.local_p2: That is the case for several video analysis and editing features, among them:
sparkle.local_p3: When you use these features locally, the material they need stays on your machine and is not sent to our servers.
sparkle.h2_cloud: When more power is needed, there is the cloud.
sparkle.cloud_p1: Some features need models too large to run comfortably on a machine.
sparkle.cloud_p2: That is the case for the generative features: creating or extending video, generating images, creating voices, music or sound effects, and other operations that need very large models.
sparkle.cloud_p3: Those features use the cloud and they are metered.
sparkle.cloud_p4: So Sparkle lets you use both routes: the machine when it is enough, the cloud when it is needed.
sparkle.project_p1: A generative feature does not produce a result you then have to rebuild by hand in the cut.
sparkle.project_p2: When something is generated, it enters the project as part of the editor.
sparkle.project_p3: A clip stays a clip. A change stays a change. An operation can be undone.
sparkle.project_p4: The result has to arrive in the cut, not stop halfway.
sparkle.control_p1: The assistant does not decide what to do with your project on its own.
sparkle.control_p3: And it can only use the functions Sparkle makes available.
sparkle.control_p4: Which means there is no second system able to change the project in ways the editor knows nothing about.
sparkle.control_p5: The AI speeds up the cut. It does not take over the cut.
sparkle.export_p1: Sparkle is built as a desktop editor, not as a web interface that depends on the cloud all the time.
sparkle.export_p2: Editing and the local features can keep working directly on your machine.
sparkle.export_p3: For export, Sparkle uses the hardware acceleration available on the machine where it can, so it makes use of the GPU and the encoders built into the device.
sparkle.export_p4: It supports the main formats and codecs used in professional video production.

how_we_build.title: How we build — Spinne Software
how_we_build.description: The assistant uses the editor's own tools, so anything it does is an ordinary change you can undo. What runs on your machine, and what needs the cloud.
how_we_build.og_title: The AI uses the same editor you use
how_we_build.og_description: We don't add AI as a second application beside it. In Sparkle the assistant uses the editor's own tools, and every change it makes is an ordinary one.
how_we_build.tw_description: Software that stays under control. The assistant uses the editor's own tools, and you can change or undo anything it does.
how_we_build.lede: We build software that stays under control.
how_we_build.lede_p2: When we add artificial intelligence to a product, we don't want to create a second application working next to the first.
how_we_build.lede_p3: We want it to be part of the product.
how_we_build.lede_p4: That is why, in Sparkle, the assistant uses the editor's own tools. It does not create a parallel project, and it does not change the video through steps the editor knows nothing about.
how_we_build.lede_p5: It can do what you can do. Only faster.
how_we_build.lede_p6: That choice makes the AI easier to understand, to control and to correct.
how_we_build.h2_control: AI should not take over the work.
how_we_build.control_p1: An assistant is useful when you can trust the result without having to watch it the whole time.
how_we_build.control_p2: So every change Sparkle makes to the project stays an ordinary editor change.
how_we_build.control_p3: You can carry on working. You can change what was done. You can undo it.
how_we_build.control_p4: We did not build a special way of going back for when the AI is working.
how_we_build.pull: The AI uses the same editor you use.
how_we_build.h2_safe: The project should be hard to break.
how_we_build.safe_p1: A modern editor can have many operations running at once: you can work while an automatic operation is still going, or a connection can drop at the worst moment.
how_we_build.safe_p2: The software has to handle those cases without losing work.
how_we_build.safe_p3: So Sparkle checks changes before applying them, and stops an older version of the project from overwriting a newer one.
how_we_build.safe_p4: If something cannot be applied safely, it is stopped.
how_we_build.safe_p5: Better a change refused than a change lost.
how_we_build.h2_models: The machine can do a lot on its own.
how_we_build.models_p1: Not everything we call AI has to go through the cloud.
how_we_build.models_p2: When an operation can run directly on the machine, we prefer that.
how_we_build.models_p3: That is the case for several of the features Sparkle uses to work on images and video: isolating subjects, segmentation, depth and mask tracking.
how_we_build.models_p4: The benefit is immediate: less waiting and, when the work stays on the machine, no upload of your footage to an outside service.
how_we_build.models_p5: When a feature does need the cloud, we use it where it is needed.
how_we_build.h2_parity: What you see should be what you export.
how_we_build.parity_p1: An editor cannot ask you to trust the preview and then surprise you during the export.
how_we_build.parity_p2: So we work to keep the project view and the final result as consistent as possible.
how_we_build.parity_p3: There are still particular cases where a transition can be rendered differently on export.
how_we_build.parity_p4: We would rather say so plainly than pretend they do not exist.
how_we_build.h2_build: Building well also means knowing what not to build.
how_we_build.build_p1: We don't develop every component from scratch.
how_we_build.build_p2: We use existing technology when it is mature and right for the problem, and we build directly what we consider important to the experience of the product.
how_we_build.build_p4: We are not interested in being able to say we wrote every line of code.
how_we_build.build_p5: We are interested in knowing why the product works the way it does.
how_we_build.cost_p1: Every technical decision is also a product decision.
how_we_build.cost_p2: A completely free AI could do more, but it would also be harder to control.
how_we_build.cost_p3: Running more work locally can improve privacy, but it also asks more of the machine.
how_we_build.cost_p4: Using outside services lets you build faster, but it introduces dependencies.
how_we_build.cost_p5: We don't try to eliminate these trade-offs.
how_we_build.cost_p6: We try to know them, and to make choices that make sense for the person using the product.
how_we_build.close_p1: We don't believe software has to be complicated to be powerful.
how_we_build.close_p2: And we don't believe artificial intelligence has to be mysterious to be useful.
how_we_build.close_p3: We build tools that do their job, that can be controlled, and that get better over time.

about.title: Company — Spinne Software
about.description: An independent Italian software company in Rome. We build and run our own products instead of contracts, and we are clear about what we don't have.
about.og_title: An independent Italian software company in Rome
about.og_description: Spinne Software builds and runs its own products instead of contracts. What exists today, which suppliers we use, and what we are not certified for.
about.tw_description: An independent Italian software company in Rome, building and running its own products. The first one is Sparkle.
about.intro_p1: Spinne Software is an independent Italian company based in Rome.
about.intro_p2: We build and run our own software products.
about.intro_p3: We are not a software house that develops applications for other companies. Our decisions, our products and the technology behind them are all part of the same business.
about.why_p1: A product does not end when it is delivered.
about.why_p2: It goes on being developed, used, fixed and improved. The work done today is still there tomorrow, both in the product and in the skills we built to make it.
about.why_p3: That is why we chose to invest in our own products instead of building the company on contract work.
about.why_p4: We want to build something that can grow over time.
about.one_p2: That keeps a direct line between the decisions and the work needed to carry them out. We have no large organisation to maintain, and we don't want to create one before it is needed.
about.one_p3: The size of the company is not a compromise on the quality of the product.
about.one_p4: It is simply how we chose to start.
about.tech_p1: We have no rule that every piece of technology has to be ours.
about.tech_p2: We build directly what we consider important to our products, and we use outside services when that is the sensible answer.
about.tech_p3: Today that means specialised suppliers for some artificial intelligence features, audio processing and payments: OpenRouter for the assistant's models, fal.ai for generative work, Deepgram and Google Cloud for speech, and Stripe for payment.
about.tech_p4: Dependencies are part of the product, so we make them visible.
about.built_p1: The first Spinne Software product is Sparkle, a desktop video editor with AI tools built to reduce repetitive work during editing.
about.built_p2: Sparkle is currently in private preview.
about.comp_p1: We think a company should be clear about what it does and what it offers.
about.comp_p2: So we describe our products for what they are, we say when a feature uses outside services, and we keep the company's details public.
about.comp_p3: The rest is part of the work behind the products.

It builds no profile of you, and nothing about you leaves here. The only data anyone receives when you read a page is the handful of technical details every web server needs in order to send it to you. They're described in full below, including the ones we'd rather not have.

This is a technical requirement of the internet, not a choice: without your IP address there is no return address to deliver the page to.
privacy.what_p2: These entries are written to the hosting provider's server logs and are used only to deliver the site and to protect it from abuse, such as denial-of-service attacks. They are never used to profile you and never combined with other data.
privacy.what_p3: We do not sell your personal information, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising, as those terms are used under California law. There is no mechanism on this site to do either.

Where that data originates in a region that restricts such transfers — the European Union, for example — the transfer relies on the providers' certification under the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework and on the European Commission's adequacy decision of 10 July 2023. Their handling of the data is described in the

privacy.absent_p1: No cookies. No local or session storage. No analytics or measurement of any kind. No advertising or tracking pixels. No embedded videos, maps or social widgets. No contact form. No newsletter. The typeface is served from this same domain rather than from a font provider, so no request about you leaves this site. There are two scripts, both served from this domain. One reads the language your browser asks for and, if this site is published in it, replaces the address with that version; the setting is read once, not stored and not sent anywhere. The other replaces the browser's bounce at the top edge of the page, and reloads the page when that edge is pulled far enough. Neither sets a cookie, uses any storage, or records anything.

answers_transcribe.title: Transcribing video without uploading — Spinne Software
answers_transcribe.description: Whisper runs on your machine. Which Sparkle setting keeps the audio there, why Auto doesn't, and what the eight-minute threshold actually decides.
answers_transcribe.og_description: Naming a local Whisper model keeps the audio on your machine. Auto sends it to a cloud engine instead. The difference, and where it lives in the code.
answers_transcribe.tw_description: Which Sparkle settings keep audio on your machine, and the one that does not.
answers_transcribe.lede: Whisper runs on your own machine. Getting from that to a subtitle file on a timeline is the part nobody writes down, and it's the part where footage quietly leaves the building.
answers_transcribe.short_a: Name a Whisper model in Sparkle — tiny, base, small, medium or large-v3-turbo. The audio never leaves your machine. Not “encrypted in transit”. Doesn't leave.
answers_transcribe.short_b: Leave the engine on Auto and the answer changes. That's the next section.
answers_transcribe.short_p: Sparkle ships two local speech engines: whisper.cpp by preference, faster-whisper when it isn't available. Both run locally, in the application's own backend.
answers_transcribe.h2_auto: When Auto does upload, and why
answers_transcribe.auto_warn_a: Auto is not local-first, at any length. With a cloud engine configured, Auto sends the audio to it — Deepgram first, Google Cloud second — whatever the length of the file. Local Whisper is what Auto falls back to when no cloud engine is configured, or when all of them fail.
answers_transcribe.auto_warn_b: The eight-minute threshold isn't the local-versus-cloud gate. Past 480 seconds, measured with ffprobe before anything is sent, the request is pinned to Deepgram and Google drops out of the chain.
answers_transcribe.auto_p1: That threshold exists because the older Google engine caps out at roughly eight minutes of audio and was never a candidate for long files. It decides which cloud engine, not whether the cloud gets used at all.
answers_transcribe.auto_p2: The fallback runs one way only. This is worth being precise about, because it's the whole promise:
auto_rules: A named local model never becomes a cloud call. The branch that talks to a cloud engine is only entered when the requested engine is a cloud engine, or is Auto. A request for small can't reach it.
A cloud engine falls back to local. If Deepgram is unconfigured, unhealthy, or fails mid-job, the work lands on local Whisper instead of failing.
answers_transcribe.auto_p3: So the setting is the whole control surface. If footage is under embargo or covered by an NDA, name the model. Don't leave it on Auto and hope.
answers_transcribe.model_p1: On Auto, when it does stay local, Sparkle uses large-v3-turbo. Naming a model explicitly overrides that, and it's the only way to get a smaller one on the automatic path.
answers_transcribe.model_p2: There's no VRAM floor to clear. Sparkle doesn't refuse to run on a machine; it takes what the machine has and degrades. The practical limit is patience, not hardware.
answers_transcribe.model_p3: Local transcription won't take the machine with it. Threads are capped at half the logical core count, and never more than eight. You can keep working while it runs.
not_items: Auto won't keep audio local, at any length. If a cloud engine is configured, Auto uses it. Name a model if that matters.
Local transcription isn't metered. Cloud transcription is, and that's the other thing the engine setting decides for you.
limits: Threshold that pins Auto to Deepgram — 480 seconds
Platforms — macOS on Apple Silicon; Windows 64-bit, in beta

answers_transcribe.back_to_sparkle: Back to what Sparkle runs on your machine
answers_transcribe.model_p4: The weights aren't inside the installer. Sparkle keeps its models in its own data folder and fetches what it needs, so the first local transcription has a download in front of it and the ones after don't.
